added_failures_note: measured by the reviewer: base arm 02a98eb0e tests/ids 569 collected 0 failed EXIT=0 (logs/review_base_arm.log), head arm 734aada5c tests/ids 571 collected 0 failed EXIT=0 (logs/review_head_arm.log); neither arm reports a FAILED or ERROR id, and the reviewed run's manifest records an after_suite at e94cedbd8 with failure_count 0 but an empty baseline_suite, so the count comes from arms the reviewer ran
call_sites: one production call site: imas_codex/ids/workers.py run_mapping_engine (workers.py:1400-1410) wires assign_worker/map_worker and the has-work lambda; no other production caller of the changed functions.

findings.text: follow-on: the map_worker idle branch now exits only when assign_phase.done and not pending, and otherwise sleeps 2.0s and re-probes. If a selected source's claim is held by a process that never releases it, the loop polls indefinitely with no attempt cap or backoff of its own, so the run ends only when the shared claim recovery elsewhere clears the claim. Section 5 explicitly asks the worker to keep polling until the source is 'claimable or recovered, so this is the intended shape rather than a defect, but the wait is unbounded in this loop and worth a bound or a log if claim recovery ever stalls.

follow-on: the new Cypher in has_pending_mapping_work (c.ids = $ids_name and NOT n.id IN $handled_source_ids) is exercised only through mocks in the gate -- tests/ids/test_map_worker_selected_homes.py patches has_pending_mapping_work and drives a MagicMock graph -- so neither the IDS filter nor the handled-source exclusion is asserted against a live graph by any test. I confirmed the statement parses and runs (EXPLAIN ok; live predicate returns has_work=true for jt-60sa magnetics against 7517 SignalSource), but the gate does not cover it.

follow-on for the coordinator: the live receipt's MAPS_TO_IMAS bindings are no longer present in the graph. A live count returns 0 MAPS_TO_IMAS edges for jt-60sa and 0 edge graph-wide, while the SignalSource label still holds 7517 nodes and the run's own log recorded 'Persisted mapping jt-60sa:magnetics with 8 bindings'. The bindings were cleared after the run by concurrent map activity (the plan has section 1 and section 6 map nodes in flight), so the run's live claim cannot be re-verified now even though its own logs and the fragment record it. Not a defect in this node's work.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against 02a98eb0e. e94cedbd8 adds one call -- 'await asyncio.to_thread(release_mapping_claim, source_id)' -- in assign_worker once select_candidates is durable, and widens has_pending_mapping_work with an ids_name filter and a handled_source_ids exclusion; map_worker's idle branch now computes a per-IDS 'pending' from has_pending_mapping_work(facility, ids_name, handled_ids) and only marks done when assign_phase.done and not pending; run_mapping_engine's has-work lambda probes every target IDS. It also adds tests/ids/test_map_worker_selected_homes.py (2 tests). 734aada5c adds the evidence fragment only.
item_verdicts.done_when: section 5's measure has three parts: the merged head passes tests/ids/test_map_worker_selected_homes.py and the mapping tests under tests/ids/; a live 'imas map run jt-60sa -i magnetics' writes at least one MAPS_TO_IMAS binding for each source that held a selected target; and a no-selected source is left unbound. Parts one is met at the pinned head: both arms I ran are green (test_map_worker_selected_homes 2 passed; tests/ids collected 571, 0 failures, EXIT=0 at head vs 569, 0 failures, EXIT=0 at base). Part two and three are met by the run's own receipt (pre-selected bound 4 and 4; three no-selected sources bound 0) quoted in the evidence fragment, though the fragment itself states the live run does not isolate the in-run release path.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal from section 5 is that the map worker takes the sources the assignment pass selected instead of exiting while they are still claimed. The diff releases the shared source claim in assign_worker once target selection is durable (workers.py:752) and keeps map_worker polling while each target IDS still has a selected, unbound home outside those already handled this run, replacing the old 'assign_phase.done or map_phase.done' exit with 'assign_phase.done and not pending' (workers.py:941-960). The mechanism matches the stated goal and is exercised by a live jt-60sa magnetics run that bound both pre-selected sources.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it records status complete, commits e94cedbd8 and 734aada5c (both ancestors of main HEAD), tests/ids 562 passed/5 skipped/4 deselected and the selected-homes gate 2 passed, a negative_control_log whose FAILED id matches its note, and an after_suite object naming revision e94cedbd8 with failure_count 0. baseline_suite is empty (it declares no base arm), so the added-failure figure below was measured from a base arm and head arm I ran at 02a98eb0e and 734aada5c.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the reviewed manifest declares imas_codex/ids/workers.py, tests/ids/test_map_worker_selected_homes.py and the evidence fragment. git diff --name-status 02a98eb0e..734aada5c lists exactly imas_codex/ids/workers.py, tests/ids/test_map_worker_selected_homes.py and docs/evidence/fragments/jt60sa-mapping-study-expansion/map-worker-takes-selected.html, every one inside the fence, with no generated model and nothing outside it.

justifications.durability: the guard is real and mutation-sensitive: the release call is asserted by the new unit test and the negative control fires. Both new decision branches have tests. Two soft spots: map_worker's idle branch can now poll every 2s without an in-loop bound if a selected source's external claim is never released, relying on claim recovery elsewhere to end it; and tests/ids/test_map_worker_selected_homes.py patches has_pending_mapping_work itself (and drives a MagicMock graph), so the new Cypher -- the ids filter and the handled-source exclusion -- is not asserted against a live graph by the gate.
justifications.evidence: I ran both arms at the pinned revisions in scratch trees under TMPDIR: head 734aada5c tests/ids collected 571, 0 failed, EXIT=0 (logs/review_head_arm.log) and base 02a98eb0e collected 569, 0 failed, EXIT=0 (logs/review_base_arm.log), so zero failures are added by the diff. I reproduced the reviewed run's declared mutation independently -- removing the release_mapping_claim call from assign_worker reddens test_assignment_releases_selected_source_for_mapping (1 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1, logs/review_negative_control.log) while the head arm passes both. The live receipt names the two pre-selected sources with their binding counts and the three no-selected controls at zero, and the evidence fragment quotes it. The gap: the run's persisted MAPS_TO_IMAS edges are no longer in the graph (a live count returns 0 for jt-60sa and 0 graph-wide while SignalSource is 7517), so the live claim is historical, not reproducible now.
justifications.fit: the change follows the module's shape -- it reuses the existing release_mapping_claim and has_pending helpers, threads new optional parameters (ids_name, handled_source_ids) through has_pending_mapping_work with status_params the helper already supports, and keeps the to_thread idiom for graph calls. The new parameters default to None so existing callers are unaffected.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the deliverable is present in the restored claim release in assign_* -- the diff releases the shared claim the moment target selection is durable (workers.py:752) and keeps map_worker polling for selected unbound homes (workers.py:941-960), which is exactly the mechanism section 5 names; the live jt-60sa magnetics run confirms the post-fix pipeline binds both pre-selected sources. The one shortfall is that the live run does not exercise the fixed in-run path (no claimable escalated source exists on jt-60sa), so the goal is met by construction and unit test, not by the live animal.
justifications.reuse: the diff reuses release_mapping_claim (already used elsewhere in map_* -- workers.py:409) rather than minting a new release path, and extends has_pending_mapping_work in place rather than adding a second probe. It extends the existing has-work lambda instead of duplicating it. No duplicated constant or parallel mechanism was introduced.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-status 02a98eb0e..734aada5c lists exactly imas_codex/ids/workers.py, tests/ids/test_map_worker_selected_homes.py and the evidence fragment, all inside the declared fence, with no generated model and nothing outside it; the manifest's changed_paths match.
